decisions.question: q-325985

authoring.question: q-325985
authoring.value:
The parametric equations of the full hyperbola are

$$
x=\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{6}\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,t\in [-\pi ,\pi ],\,t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-hyperbola, we refer to the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14053984/assets/6ac31692404208d80637291fb30be028a7efdc3a172af0337da26039f1e87326.png)

We can see that if we restrict $t$ to $[-\pi ,-\frac{\pi }{2}),$ we get only the quarter-hyperbola.

Therefore, the parametric equations that describe the required quarter-hyperbola are

$$
x=\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{6}\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,t\in [-\pi ,-\frac{\pi }{2}).
$$

authoring.value:
The parametric equations of the full hyperbola are

$$
x=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,t\in [-\pi ,\pi ],\,t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a single branch, we refer to the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14064533/assets/b43dcf6c343994e3226e2840a0ae80f60484c8de5d7984f61ec6447185181a76.png)

We can see that if we restrict $t$ to $(-\frac{\pi }{2},0]$ and $[0,\frac{\pi }{2}),$ we get only the right branch.

Therefore, the parametric equations that describe only the right branch are

$$
x=4\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=7\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}).
$$

decisions.question: e-7896

authoring.question: e-7896
authoring.value:
The parametric equations of the full hyperbola are

$$
x= \sqrt2 \sec{t}, \quad
y = \sqrt3 \tan{t}, \quad
t \in [-\pi,\pi], \quad
t \neq \pm\dfrac{\pi}2.
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-hyperbola, we refer to the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14053984/assets/730325137cfca58eb17d65103e539d084f81d7ab810628261125c29dbb8a0284.png)

We can see that if we restrict $t$ to $\left[0, \dfrac{\pi}2\right)$ we get the required quarter-hyperbola.

Therefore, the parametric equations that describe the required quarter-hyperbola are

$$
x= \sqrt2\sec{t}, \quad
y = \sqrt3\tan{t}, \quad
t \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}2\right).
$$
